subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should deep audit enforce a 1 MiB maximum installed-plugin manifest size and report larger manifests through the existing parse-warning plus whole-directory fallback path?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but the accepted manifest-size boundary and the resulting scan coverage for oversized legitimate manifests are security-policy choices owned by the repository.

options.title: Approve the 1 MiB boundary
options.body: Retain the current cap and warning/fallback behavior, then merge once exact-head required checks are acceptable.

options.title: Choose a different boundary
options.body: Request a different fixed limit or finding classification if legitimate plugin manifests require more headroom.

recommendation.title: Approve the 1 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Retain the current cap and warning/fallback behavior, then merge once exact-head required checks are acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: This team is the explicit CODEOWNER for the changed security-audit path.
